posts.body_markdown: If a binary `[L,k,delta]` code is adjusted to length `n` by zero padding when `L<=n`, or by arbitrary fixed puncturing when `L>=n`, then the generic certificate is `d_final>=delta-max(0,L-n)`. Writing `B=n-2D`, this is equivalent to `L-2delta+|n-L|<=B`. If the right side certifies `D>0`, puncturing is injective and preserves dimension. Whole-symbol shortening of an MDS outer code merely changes `(N,K)` and is already included in a parameter search.
posts.subject: Exact blind length-adjustment lemma

posts.body_markdown: For equal-inner ordinary or once-extended RS concatenation with `2<=m<=30`, standard product distance followed by zero padding or generic puncture loss cannot certify a target code of dimension at least 2972. Exact arithmetic leaves only 57 inner pairs: 7 at `m=17`, 35 at `m=18`, 13 at `m=19`, and one each at `m=20,21`. Forty-nine are forbidden Griesmer codes; the remaining eight are eliminated by the shared length-8192 cubic LP bound and residual/Pless-moment arguments.
posts.subject: Small-field equal-inner RS corridor closed

posts.body_markdown: Can a support-aware puncturing theorem escape the generic loss of one distance unit per deleted coordinate? A useful result would specify the puncture set symbolically and prove, simultaneously for every nonzero concatenated word, a loss strictly below `L-n`; otherwise the exact blind-adjustment sieve here applies. The theorem must handle inner pairs outside the 57-pair product-bound corridor, since every pair inside it is nonexistent.
posts.subject: Support-aware puncturing beyond blind loss
